NetCoreNOC feedback-dataset bias report
==============================================================

This report MEASURES. It trains nothing, fits nothing, and recommends
no model. Every figure below is an aggregate.

-- THE EVIDENCE BOUNDARY (read this first) -------------------
label rows: reported != reconciled               0
  marks that difference accounts for             0
marks the CLIENT reported (untrusted)            1
marks the SERVER reconciled                      1
  of those, derived by migration 0011            0

  A NUMBER THAT DESCRIBES THE EVIDENCE IS DERIVED BY THE SERVER; a
  number that describes the client may be derived from the client. The
  marked ids are what an operator's browser SENT, and until v0.9.2 their
  raw count was multiplied into the asserted-negative total below — so a
  label marking ids that named no member of its bag could move that total
  while asserting nothing at all. The reconciled count is the reported
  set intersected with the server's own bag, computed at the verdict.
  A NON-ZERO FIRST LINE means some label was written by something other
  than the shipped UI. Nothing is corrected on its account: a
  disagreement is evidence about a write path, and repairing the row
  would destroy it.

-- SCOPE OF THE ASSERTION (never averaged) -------------------
  clean   (nothing was hidden)                   0
  checked (restricted, and measured)             0
  unknown (no scope was recorded)                1
marks about members not observable               0

  A scoped editor may mark a member they were never shown — the
  redaction carries no alarm id, so the ids are guessable — and the
  resulting assertion is one they were not in a position to make. It is
  still recorded: this makes it LEGIBLE, it does not prevent it.
  The three populations are counted SEPARATELY and never averaged. An
  `unknown` row is one whose scope was never recorded — every label
  written before migration 0011, plus any written through a path that
  resolved none. It is permanently uninterpretable and is NOT assumed to
  be clean; assuming would invent an observation nobody made.

-- corpus ----------------------------------------------------
pairs, sink (awaiting a label)                   0
pairs, dataset (promoted by a label)             8
observations, sink                               9
observations, dataset                            0
capture runs                                     1

  of those, inside the training window           8
  outside it (held, not selectable)              0
  ORPHANED: promoted, label since gone           0

  The training window SELECTS; it does not delete. Nothing dies at that
  boundary — a training-retention delete would destroy evidence to express
  a modelling preference, and selection is a WHERE clause. So the corpus
  has two sizes: what it HOLDS and what a model may READ.
  An ORPHANED pair is a promoted pair whose label no longer exists — a
  feature nothing can interpret. It is counted, never collected: the
  corpus is not corrupt, its USABLE size is just smaller than its row
  count. Sources are an audit-bound reduction landing between a label and
  its features, and any pre-v0.8.1 database that lost labels to F44.

-- the machine's decision (NOT a label) -----------------------
pairs the incumbent linked                       5  (62.5%)
accepted links dropped by the cap                1
pairs evaluated during a storm                   2  (25.0%)

  `incumbent_linked` is the champion's decision at that instant. It is
  provenance and a legitimate feature. It is NOT a target, and no metric
  that decides promotion may be computed against it: a challenger judged
  by the champion can only converge on it. Its class balance is also a
  property of the TRAFFIC, not of the scorer — measured at 0% accept on
  quiet corpus traffic and 100% in a storm.

-- human labels ----------------------------------------------
confirm                                          3
split                                            3
total                                            6

-- INFORMATIVENESS (what a label ASSERTS, not how many there are) --
ASSERTED NEGATIVE PAIRS (reconciled)             2
  splits: plain (no boundary named)              2
  splits: partial (boundary named)               1
  exclusions truncated at the bound              0
  asserted negatives per label        n=1 min=2 med=2 p90=2 max=2 mean=2.0
  |marked| / bag size, in tenths      n=1 min=3 med=3 p90=3 max=3 mean=3.0
remainder assertion: offered                     1
remainder assertion: taken                       0
pairs left UNASSERTED in those bags              1

  BEFORE v0.9.1 THE FIRST NUMBER WAS ZERO FOR EVERY CORPUS THAT HAS
  EVER EXISTED. A `split` asserted that the bag was at least two
  situations WITHOUT SAYING WHICH, so it supported no pairwise claim at
  all — which is why `split_bag_intact_rate` had to be a separately
  named quantity rather than an over-merge rate with a denominator.

  A partial split asserts `marked` x `rest` NEGATIVE and NOTHING ELSE.
  The pairs within the remainder and within the marked set are UNKNOWN,
  not positive — the operator did not speak about them. The last line
  counts exactly those, and it is printed beside the negatives so that a
  later release cannot read 'not asserted positive' as 'asserted
  negative'. The identity closes: m*r + r(r-1)/2 + m(m-1)/2 = n(n-1)/2.

  `offered` and `taken` are BOTH ZERO by construction while the shipped
  UI has no control for the remainder assertion (DECISIONS #127) — a
  rate over an affordance nobody was given is not a measurement of
  operators, so it is named rather than quietly omitted.

-- ACQUISITION CHANNELS (NEVER averaged together) -------------
close                                            1
  confirm / split                            1 / 0
  of the splits, partial                         0
  asserted neg. pairs (reconciled)               0
  marks the client reported                      0
  under a restricting scope                      0
  carrying a client report                       0
organic                                          4
  confirm / split                            2 / 2
  of the splits, partial                         1
  asserted neg. pairs (reconciled)               2
  marks the client reported                      1
  under a restricting scope                      1
  carrying a client report                       1
unrecorded                                       1
  confirm / split                            0 / 1
  of the splits, partial                         0
  asserted neg. pairs (reconciled)               0
  marks the client reported                      0
  under a restricting scope                      0
  carrying a client report                       0

  `organic` is a label an operator gave while browsing. `close` is one
  given while RESOLVING a situation, and that selects for resolved
  incidents — a DIFFERENT POPULATION, not a bigger sample of the same
  one. Blending them would destroy the bias characterisation
  retroactively, for rows already written, which is why the column has
  existed unused since v0.8.0 and why every figure above is repeated
  per channel rather than averaged.

-- JUDGEMENT NOT CAPTURED ------------------------------------
situations closed                                0
  closed WITH a verdict                          0
  closed WITHOUT one                             0

  Every situation in the last line is a judgement an operator made and
  the product failed to record. It is the quantity Workstream 2 aims
  at, and v0.9.1's Gate 0 could not measure it on any corpus this
  repository can construct — the corpus labels every situation by
  construction, and not one of its closes came from an operator. It is
  counted here from the day this release ships so that the release
  which needs the number can have it.

-- EFFECTIVE SAMPLE SIZE -------------------------------------
independent bags (n)                             6
distinct operators                               2
distinct incidents (merge-aware)                 4
labels with no recorded operator                 1

  *n* IS THE NUMBER OF INDEPENDENT BAGS, NOT THE NUMBER OF PAIRS.
  Pairs from one alarm share a side; pairs from one situation are strongly
  correlated; situations from one operator share a criterion. A report
  quoting the pair count would produce confidence intervals wrong by a
  factor nobody checks.

-- bag sizes -------------------------------------------------
members per labelled bag              n=5 min=0 med=2 p90=3 max=3 mean=2.0
bags with zero members                           1

  CONFIRMATION STRENGTH DECAYS WITH BAG SIZE. An operator confirming a
  twenty-member situation did not verify one hundred and ninety pairs;
  one confirming two members verified the only pair there was. This
  distribution is what lets a later release weight rather than assume.
  A zero-member bag is a verdict on an already-merged situation: real,
  recorded, and not interchangeable with the rest.

-- operator concentration ------------------------------------
share from the single top operator           60.0%
share from the top three                    100.0%

  A dataset that is three people's judgement is a dataset about three
  people.

-- visibility scope ------------------------------------------
labels made under a restricting scope            1
redacted members among those          n=1 min=2 med=2 p90=2 max=2 mean=2.0

  A scoped editor labels a PARTIAL VIEW and cannot say which part. The
  resulting noise is SYSTEMATIC, not random: it correlates with the scope
  policy, so it does not average out with more data.

-- label latency ---------------------------------------------
seconds, situation open to verdict    n=5 min=30 med=117 p90=599 max=599 mean=192.6

  Also how the sink's 21-day default gets tested against reality. That
  default is a conservative GUESS; this distribution is what replaces it.

-- coverage --------------------------------------------------
situations known (live + labelled)               4
situations that received a label                 4
  as a rate                                 100.0%
evaluated pairs ever promoted               100.0%
per-label coverage: full                         3
per-label coverage: partial                      0
per-label coverage: none                         1
per-label coverage: empty                        1

  The denominator is every situation this database has EVIDENCE of: those
  still in `situation`, plus those named by a surviving label. It is not
  `COUNT(*) FROM situation`, which the operational prune shrinks while
  labels outlive it — that denominator printed 300.0% before v0.8.1. This
  one contains its own numerator by construction, so no clamp is needed.

  `partial` is NOT an edge case. The sliding window and MAX_CANDIDATES
  mean pairs within a labelled situation may never have been evaluated —
  a nine-member situation has thirty-six pairs. Recorded rather than
  silently dropped, which is the censoring this release exists to end.
  `empty` is a verdict on a situation with no members — a fourth state the
  specification's three did not anticipate, because all three presuppose a bag.

-- provenance (NEVER averaged together) -----------------------
current                                          5
legacy_capture                                   1

  `legacy_capture` rows were acquired before v0.7.5 repaired the click
  path. They are NOT known to be bad — they are of UNKNOWN QUALITY, which
  is a weaker and different claim. Excluded from training by default,
  includable by an explicit choice, and never blended into the figures
  above without saying so.

-- acquisition channel ---------------------------------------
close                                            1
organic                                          4
unrecorded                                       1
-- operator gestures (v0.16.0) --------------------------------
producing training rows                          0

-- membership divergence -------------------------------------
labels carrying a client report                  1
client bag differs from the server               1
client report truncated                          0

  This is a METRIC, not an error: the residual race v0.7.5 narrowed but
  did not eliminate, measured rather than assumed. The server's bag is
  authoritative; the client's is evidence.

-- leakage exposure ------------------------------------------
dataset pairs evaluated after label 1            0
distinct matrix epochs in the dataset            1
observations                                     9
  distinct alarms among them                     9

  A human verdict mutates A and E, so a pair evaluated afterwards carries
  features that already contain information from an earlier label. Note
  the mechanism: the label does NOT advance the epoch (since v0.7.1's F36
  fix, only a closed situation does) — the contamination travels through
  the MASS VALUES. Observations sharing an alarm id are re-fires of one
  deduplicated alarm and are near-duplicates, not independent samples.

-- retention state -------------------------------------------
sink_days                                     21.0
sink_rows                                  2000000
training_days                                365.0
audit_days                                   730.0
span of surviving labels (days)                0.0

  Pruning a training corpus is CENSORING BY POLICY. It is legitimate and
  it must be visible: a model trained under twelve months' retention and
  one trained under three are not comparable, and nothing else would
  record which was which.

-- what this report CANNOT tell you --------------------------
  * whether a verdict was correct. There is no ground truth here, only
    what an operator said.
  * whether the labels are representative of the network. Operators
    label what they open, and this measures what they labelled.
  * which of the `legacy_capture` rows are actually bad. Nothing
    recorded it, which is precisely why they are marked and not deleted.
  * anything about pairs that were never evaluated. They are absent by
    construction; `partial` coverage counts them, and that is all.
